passages.label: Inferno I.1-3
passages.quote:
Midway upon the journey of our life
I found myself within a forest dark,
For the straightforward pathway had been lost.

passages.label: Inferno I.4-6
passages.quote:
Ah me! how hard a thing it is to say
What was this forest savage, rough, and stern,
Which in the very thought renews the fear.

passages.label: Inferno III.9
passages.quote: All hope abandon, ye who enter in!

passages.label: Inferno III.22-24
passages.quote:
There sighs, complaints, and ululations loud
Resounded through the air without a star,
Whence I, at the beginning, wept thereat.

passages.label: Inferno XXXIV.139
passages.quote: Thence we came forth to rebehold the stars.

passages.label: Paradise Lost I.1-6
passages.quote:
Of Mans First Disobedience, and the Fruit
Of that Forbidden Tree, whose mortal tast
Brought Death into the World, and all our woe,
With loss of Eden, till one greater Man
Restore us, and regain the blissful Seat,
Sing Heav'nly Muse.

passages.label: Paradise Lost I.105-109
passages.quote:
What though the field be lost?
All is not lost; the unconquerable Will,
And study of revenge, immortal hate,
And courage never to submit or yield:
And what is else not to be overcome?

passages.label: Paradise Lost I.254-255
passages.quote:
The mind is its own place, and in it self
Can make a Heav'n of Hell, a Hell of Heav'n.

passages.label: Paradise Lost I.263
passages.quote: Better to reign in Hell, then serve in Heav'n.

passages.label: Paradise Lost II.432-433
passages.quote:
Long is the way
And hard, that out of Hell leads up to light.

passages.label: Songs of Experience: The Tyger 1-4
passages.quote:
Tyger Tyger, burning bright,
In the forests of the night;
What immortal hand or eye,
Could frame thy fearful symmetry?

passages.label: Songs of Experience: The Tyger 17-20
passages.quote:
When the stars threw down their spears
And water'd heaven with their tears:
Did he smile his work to see?
Did he who made the Lamb make thee?

passages.label: Songs of Experience: The Sick Rose 1-4
passages.quote:
O Rose thou art sick.
The invisible worm,
That flies in the night
In the howling storm:

passages.label: Songs of Experience: The Sick Rose 5-8
passages.quote:
Has found out thy bed
Of crimson joy:
And his dark secret love
Does thy life destroy.

passages.label: Songs of Experience: London 1-4
passages.quote:
I wander thro' each charter'd street,
Near where the charter'd Thames does flow.
And mark in every face I meet
Marks of weakness, marks of woe.

works.title: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
works.author: William Blake

passages.label: Proverbs of Hell
passages.quote: The road of excess leads to the palace of wisdom.

passages.label: Proverbs of Hell
passages.quote: The tygers of wrath are wiser than the horses of instruction.

passages.label: A Memorable Fancy, plate 14
passages.quote: If the doors of perception were cleansed every thing would appear to man as it is, Infinite.

passages.label: Proverbs of Hell
passages.quote: What is now proved was once, only imagin'd.

passages.label: Proverbs of Hell
passages.quote: Eternity is in love with the productions of time.

passages.label: The Raven 1-4
passages.quote:
Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary,
Over many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore—
While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping,
As of some one gently rapping, rapping at my chamber door.

passages.label: The Raven 25-26
passages.quote:
Deep into that darkness peering, long I stood there wondering, fearing,
Doubting, dreaming dreams no mortal ever dared to dream before.

passages.label: The Raven 48
passages.quote: Quoth the Raven "Nevermore."

passages.label: The Raven 103-106
The Raven 107-108
passages.quote:
And my soul from out that shadow that lies floating on the floor
Shall be lifted—nevermore!

passages.label: Frankenstein, Letter 1
passages.quote: You will rejoice to hear that no disaster has accompanied the commencement of an enterprise which you have regarded with such evil forebodings.

passages.label: Frankenstein, Chapter 5
passages.quote: It was on a dreary night of November that I beheld the accomplishment of my toils.

passages.label: Frankenstein, Chapter 5
passages.quote: I saw the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathed hard, and a convulsive motion agitated its limbs.

passages.label: Frankenstein, Chapter 20
passages.quote: Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.

passages.label: Frankenstein, Chapter 17
passages.quote: I am malicious because I am miserable.

passages.label: Ozymandias 1-3
passages.quote:
I met a traveller from an antique land,
Who said—"Two vast and trunkless legs of stone
Stand in the desert. . . ."

passages.label: Ozymandias 3-6
passages.quote:
Near them, on the sand,
Half sunk a shattered visage lies, whose frown,
And wrinkled lip, and sneer of cold command,
Tell that its sculptor well those passions read

passages.label: Ozymandias 9-11
Ozymandias 12-14
passages.quote:
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay
Of that colossal Wreck, boundless and bare
The lone and level sands stretch far away.

works.title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
works.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge

passages.label: Rime I.1-4
passages.quote:
It is an ancient Mariner,
And he stoppeth one of three.
'By thy long grey beard and glittering eye,
Now wherefore stopp'st thou me?'

passages.label: Rime II.119-122
passages.quote:
Water, water, every where,
And all the boards did shrink;
Water, water, every where,
Nor any drop to drink.

passages.label: Rime IV.232-235
passages.quote:
Alone, alone, all, all alone,
Alone on a wide wide sea!
And never a saint took pity on
My soul in agony.

passages.label: Rime VII.614-617
passages.quote:
He prayeth best, who loveth best
All things both great and small;
For the dear God who loveth us,
He made and loveth all.

passages.label: Rime VII.624-625
passages.quote:
A sadder and a wiser man,
He rose the morrow morn.

passages.label: Kubla Khan 1-5
passages.quote:
In Xanadu did Kubla Khan
A stately pleasure-dome decree:
Where Alph, the sacred river, ran
Through caverns measureless to man
Down to a sunless sea.

passages.label: Kubla Khan 14-16
passages.quote:
A savage place! as holy and enchanted
As e'er beneath a waning moon was haunted
By woman wailing for her demon-lover!

passages.label: Kubla Khan 29-30
passages.quote:
And 'mid this tumult Kubla heard from far
Ancestral voices prophesying war!

passages.label: Kubla Khan 48-52
passages.quote:
And all who heard should see them there,
And all should cry, Beware! Beware!
His flashing eyes, his floating hair!
Weave a circle round him thrice,
And close your eyes with holy dread,

passages.label: Ode to a Nightingale 1-4
passages.quote:
My heart aches, and a drowsy numbness pains
My sense, as though of hemlock I had drunk,
Or emptied some dull opiate to the drains
One minute past, and Lethe-wards had sunk:

passages.label: Ode to a Nightingale 21-24
passages.quote:
Fade far away, dissolve, and quite forget
What thou among the leaves hast never known,
The weariness, the fever, and the fret
Here, where men sit and hear each other groan;

passages.label: Ode to a Nightingale 51-54
passages.quote:
Darkling I listen; and, for many a time
I have been half in love with easeful Death,
Called him soft names in many a mused rhyme,
To take into the air my quiet breath;

passages.label: Ode to a Nightingale 61-62
passages.quote:
Thou wast not born for death, immortal Bird!
No hungry generations tread thee down;

passages.label: Ode to a Nightingale 79-80
passages.quote:
Was it a vision, or a waking dream?
Fled is that music:—Do I wake or sleep?

passages.label: La Belle Dame sans Merci 1-4
passages.quote:
O what can ail thee, knight-at-arms,
Alone and palely loitering?
The sedge has wither'd from the lake,
And no birds sing.

passages.label: La Belle Dame sans Merci 13-16
passages.quote:
I met a lady in the meads,
Full beautiful—a faery's child,
Her hair was long, her foot was light,
And her eyes were wild.

passages.label: La Belle Dame sans Merci 37-40
passages.quote:
I saw pale kings and princes too,
Pale warriors, death-pale were they all;
They cried—"La Belle Dame sans Merci
Hath thee in thrall!"

passages.label: La Belle Dame sans Merci 45-48
passages.quote:
And this is why I sojourn here,
Alone and palely loitering,
Though the sedge is wither'd from the lake,
And no birds sing.

passages.label: Moby-Dick, Chapter 1
passages.quote: Call me Ishmael.

passages.label: Moby-Dick, Chapter 1
passages.quote: Whenever I find myself growing grim about the mouth; whenever it is a damp, drizzly November in my soul; whenever I find myself involuntarily pausing before coffin warehouses, and bringing up the rear of every funeral I meet; then, I account it high time to get to sea as soon as I can.

passages.label: Moby-Dick, Chapter 36
passages.quote: All visible objects, man, are but as pasteboard masks. But in each event—in the living act, the undoubted deed—there, some unknown but still reasoning thing puts forth the mouldings of its features from behind the unreasoning mask.

passages.label: Moby-Dick, Chapter 135
passages.quote: From hell's heart I stab at thee; for hate's sake I spit my last breath at thee.

passages.label: Moby-Dick, Epilogue
passages.quote: And I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

passages.label: Darkness 1-3
passages.quote:
I had a dream, which was not all a dream.
The bright sun was extinguish'd, and the stars
Did wander darkling in the eternal space,

passages.label: Darkness 6-8
Darkness 69-71
passages.quote:
The world was void,
The populous and the powerful was a lump,
Seasonless, herbless, treeless, manless, lifeless—

passages.label: Darkness 81-82
passages.quote:
Darkness had no need
Of aid from them—She was the Universe.

passages.label: Young Goodman Brown, opening forest path
passages.quote: With this excellent resolve for the future, Goodman Brown felt himself justified in making more haste on his present evil purpose.

passages.label: Young Goodman Brown, the lonely road
passages.quote: There may be a devilish Indian behind every tree, said Goodman Brown to himself; and he glanced fearfully behind him as he added, What if the devil himself should be at my very elbow!

passages.label: Young Goodman Brown, wilderness
passages.quote: The road grew wilder and drearier and more faintly traced, and vanished at length, leaving him in the heart of the dark wilderness.

passages.label: Young Goodman Brown, conclusion
passages.quote: A stern, a sad, a darkly meditative, a distrustful, if not a desperate man did he become from the night of that fearful dream.

passages.label: Song of Myself 1.4-5
passages.quote:
I loafe and invite my soul,
I lean and loafe at my ease observing a spear of summer grass.

passages.label: Song of Myself 5.1-2
passages.quote:
I believe in you my soul, the other I am must not abase itself to you,
And you must not be abased to the other.

passages.label: Song of Myself 2.1-2
passages.quote:
The smoke of my own breath,
Echoes, ripples, buzz'd whispers, love-root, silk-thread, crotch and vine,

passages.label: Song of Myself 52.6-7
passages.quote:
I depart as air, I shake my white locks at the runaway sun,
I effuse my flesh in eddies, and drift it in lacy jags.

passages.label: Goblin Market 1-4
passages.quote:
Morning and evening
Maids heard the goblins cry:
"Come buy our orchard fruits,
Come buy, come buy:"

passages.label: Goblin Market 42-45
passages.quote:
We must not look at goblin men,
We must not buy their fruits:
Who knows upon what soil they fed
Their hungry thirsty roots?

passages.label: Goblin Market 134-136
Goblin Market 562-567
passages.quote:
For there is no friend like a sister
In calm or stormy weather;
To cheer one on the tedious way,
To fetch one if one goes astray,
To lift one if one totters down,
To strengthen whilst one stands.

passages.label: Ecclesiastes 1.2
passages.quote: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

passages.label: Ecclesiastes 1.4
passages.quote: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.

passages.label: Ecclesiastes 3.1
passages.quote: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

passages.label: Ecclesiastes 3.2
passages.quote: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;

passages.label: Ecclesiastes 1.18
passages.quote: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.

passages.label: Revelation 6.8
passages.quote: And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him.

passages.label: Revelation 6.13
passages.quote: And the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, even as a fig tree casteth her untimely figs, when she is shaken of a mighty wind.

passages.label: Revelation 12.7
passages.quote: And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,

passages.label: Revelation 21.4
passages.quote: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

passages.label: "Because I could not stop for Death" 1-4
passages.quote:
Because I could not stop for Death—
He kindly stopped for me—
The Carriage held but just Ourselves—
And Immortality.

passages.label: "I heard a Fly buzz" 1-4
passages.quote:
I heard a Fly buzz—when I died—
The Stillness in the Room
Was like the Stillness in the Air—
Between the Heaves of Storm—

passages.label: "There's a certain Slant of light" 1-4
passages.quote:
There's a certain Slant of light,
Winter Afternoons—
That oppresses, like the Heft
Of Cathedral Tunes—

passages.label: "I'm Nobody! Who are you?" 1-2
passages.quote:
I'm Nobody! Who are you?
Are you—Nobody—too?

passages.label: "Hope is the thing with feathers" 1-4
passages.quote:
"Hope" is the thing with feathers—
That perches in the soul—
And sings the tune without the words—
And never stops—at all—
